parameters.toolDescription: ASYNC step 1 of 3. Start an Apify actor run and return immediately, do NOT wait. Primary Naukri actor blackfalcondata~naukri-jobs-feed (id xYOP3UjaS8w38lWM7); memo23~naukri-scraper (EYXvM0o2lS7rYzgey) fallback. Inputs: actorId, inputJson (full actor input object as a JSON string). Returns run JSON with data.id (runId) and data.defaultDatasetId. Next poll get_run_status(runId) until SUCCEEDED then get_dataset_items(datasetId).

ASYNC step 2 of 3. Check an Apify run status, returns fast. Input runId from start_actor. Returns data.status (READY, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT) and data.defaultDatasetId. Poll until SUCCEEDED, cap ~40 tries. On FAILED/ABORTED/TIMED-OUT stop and report, never fake an empty success. When SUCCEEDED call get_dataset_items(datasetId).

ASYNC step 3 of 3. Fetch rows from a finished run dataset. Input datasetId (defaultDatasetId from start_actor/get_run_status). Call ONLY after get_run_status shows SUCCEEDED. Returns the items array. Beyond 1000 rows page with &offset= and &limit=.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ slug: $fromAI("slug", "Ads2Publish publication slug, e.g. times-of-india or dainik-jagran", "string") }) }}
parameters.toolDescription: Fetch one day's recruitment ads for a single publication from Ads2Publish, parsed server-side from raw HTML so no ads are lost. Input: slug (e.g. times-of-india, dainik-jagran, eenadu). Returns classifiedCount, displayCount, highestAdIndex, missingIndices (should always be empty; a non-empty value means the source itself skipped an ad number) and ads[] with adType, adIndex, body, category (full path), email, phone. Use this instead of WebFetch, which silently drops ads.
